events.text: 9 more orders double-charged — submitting the P0 mitigation now: disable retries on the non-idempotent charge creation, citing F1–F5.

steps: PROPOSE ONLY (human approves/applies): Immediately set resilience4j.retry.instances.paymentGateway.max-attempts from 3 to 1 in config/application.yml (effectively disabling retry for paymentGateway), via hot config reload if available, otherwise a rolling restart of billing-service. This is the smallest reversible change; reverting to 3 restores prior behaviour. Do not wait for a code deploy.

If max-attempts=1 cannot take effect within minutes while duplicates continue, temporarily pause new charge captures (stop accepting createCharge calls) until the config is live — preferable to continuing duplicate captures; keep GET /v1/charges reads and webhook receipt running.
Keep the circuit breaker unchanged and do NOT pause webhooks: webhooks are reconciliation evidence, not the cause; pausing them would not stop captures (F4).

Optionally, after retries are disabled, consider raising gateway read-timeout above the gateway's degraded p99 as a secondary human-approved tuning step only — this does not replace disabling retry, since any timeout on this non-idempotent POST can still duplicate (F3).

Verify for at least 10-15 minutes: no new 'Retry paymentGateway' WARN lines (per F5 pattern), and no new orderId with >1 distinct chargeId in gateway-webhooks.log (per F4 pattern); then declare bleeding stopped.

For already-affected orders (61 reported plus 9 more per Finance update): reconcile each via GET /v1/charges?metadata.orderId=... (per gateway notes F3) and have Finance/human operators approve refunds/voids of the duplicate chargeIds — do not auto-refund without approval.
events.rationale: Root mechanism evidenced, not just hypothesized: GatewayClient.createCharge retries the non-idempotent POST /v1/charges with no Idempotency-Key header (F1); config retries it up to 3 attempts on SocketTimeoutException/IOException against a 2s read-timeout (F2); gateway docs state POST /v1/charges is not idempotent by default and a client timeout does not mean the charge failed (F3). Logs confirm timeout->retry->eventual success at 18:05 onset (F5), and webhooks show ord_90517 got 3 distinct succeeded charges of the same amount, matching 3 attempts (F4), while ord_90502/ord_90544 show 2. Gateway latency was degraded above the 2s timeout, so each timed-out (but actually completed) attempt created a new charge. Disabling retry (max-attempts=1) stops new duplicates immediately, is config-only, low-risk and fully reversible, and is safer than only raising the timeout. Permanent fix (stable Idempotency-Key per order on createCharge, retry only with that key / reconcile before retry) follows separately via submit_fix after mitigation.

steps: PROPOSE ONLY (human approves/applies): Immediately set resilience4j.retry.instances.paymentGateway.max-attempts from 3 to 1 in config/application.yml (effectively disabling retry for paymentGateway), via hot config reload if available, otherwise a rolling restart of billing-service. This is the smallest reversible change; reverting to 3 restores prior behaviour. Do not wait for a code deploy.

If max-attempts=1 cannot take effect within minutes while duplicates continue, temporarily pause new charge captures (stop accepting createCharge calls) until the config is live — preferable to continuing duplicate captures; keep GET /v1/charges reads and webhook receipt running.
Keep the circuit breaker unchanged and do NOT pause webhooks: webhooks are reconciliation evidence, not the cause; pausing them would not stop captures (F4).

Optionally, after retries are disabled, consider raising gateway read-timeout above the gateway's degraded p99 as a secondary human-approved tuning step only — this does not replace disabling retry, since any timeout on this non-idempotent POST can still duplicate (F3).

Verify for at least 10-15 minutes: no new 'Retry paymentGateway' WARN lines (per F5 pattern), and no new orderId with >1 distinct chargeId in gateway-webhooks.log (per F4 pattern); then declare bleeding stopped.

For already-affected orders (61 reported plus 9 more per Finance update): reconcile each via GET /v1/charges?metadata.orderId=... (per gateway notes F3) and have Finance/human operators approve refunds/voids of the duplicate chargeIds — do not auto-refund without approval.
mitigations.rationale: Root mechanism evidenced, not just hypothesized: GatewayClient.createCharge retries the non-idempotent POST /v1/charges with no Idempotency-Key header (F1); config retries it up to 3 attempts on SocketTimeoutException/IOException against a 2s read-timeout (F2); gateway docs state POST /v1/charges is not idempotent by default and a client timeout does not mean the charge failed (F3). Logs confirm timeout->retry->eventual success at 18:05 onset (F5), and webhooks show ord_90517 got 3 distinct succeeded charges of the same amount, matching 3 attempts (F4), while ord_90502/ord_90544 show 2. Gateway latency was degraded above the 2s timeout, so each timed-out (but actually completed) attempt created a new charge. Disabling retry (max-attempts=1) stops new duplicates immediately, is config-only, low-risk and fully reversible, and is safer than only raising the timeout. Permanent fix (stable Idempotency-Key per order on createCharge, retry only with that key / reconcile before retry) follows separately via submit_fix after mitigation.

conclusion.summary: Stop duplicate charges by having humans set paymentGateway max-attempts 3→1 immediately; root cause is retrying the non-idempotent POST /v1/charges without an Idempotency-Key when gateway latency exceeded the 2s timeout.
conclusion.root_cause: BILL-877 (Oct 24, F11) added @Retry to GatewayClient.createCharge: POST /v1/charges is not idempotent by default and timeout does not mean failure (F3), the client sends no Idempotency-Key (F1,F17) though the gateway would dedupe with it (F18), and it does not GET-reconcile before retry (F20). This stayed latent until gateway p99 rose to 2.5-3.2s from 18:04 (F9), exceeding the 2s read-timeout (F19,F2) with max-attempts 3 (F21). From first timeout-retry at 18:05:41 (F8), each retry re-captured a charge that had already succeeded server-side, producing distinct chargeIds for the same order/amount — 2 for ord_90502 (F7,F10), 3 for ord_90517 matching 3 attempts (F4,F12), 2 for ord_90544 after 1 retry (F14,F23) — while low-latency no-retry orders captured once (F6,F16).
